newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to propose auto insurance premium cuts - paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan to propose auto insurance premium cuts - paper.

text.p: A Japanese government body will propose slashing premiums for compulsory automobile liability insurance by as much as 10 percent from May, Japanese media reported Monday.
The reduction, the first since April 1993, would come partly as the result of increases in net premium income -- their premium receipts minus benefit payments, the reports said.

The Compulsory Automobile Liability Insurance Council, an advisory body to the Finance Minister, which met earlier today, will finalise the proposal at its next meeting to be held on February 4, the reports said.
Deregulation of Japan's automobile insurance premiums was one of the areas prodded by the United States in the U.S.-Japan insurance talks last year.
In February, an insurance industry body charged with setting auto insurance premium rates, will work out the details, such as the margin of the cut and the timing of its implementation.

The ministry said in the statement that the council has discussed whether to allow six major life insurers to sell mandatory automobile liability insurance policies through their nonlife insurance subsidiaries.
Media reports said that the life insurers were seeking to sell those products through their subsidiaries from April.
